newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares end up, piggyback on Reliance bonus.
newsitem.headline: India shares end up, piggyback on Reliance bonus.

text.p: ** (1230 GMT)- Indian blue chips stage smart recovery from
day's lows after news of Reliance Industries bonus meet
on June 26 bolsters market sentiment, traders say
** Shares of Reliance end 19.50 rupees, or six pct up at
340.50 after bonus news; 8.97 million shares traded
** Bombay's top 30-share index ends 6.48 pts higher at
** SBI shares steady at 339.0 rupees after firm announces
1996/97 net at 13.29 bln rupees vs 8.32 bln year ago
--net profit slightly lower than expectations, traders
** Delhi share index up 3.16 pts at 861.11, Madras gains
70.53 pts at 4,195.44 and Calcutta 0.20 pts at 115.65

The announcement of a surprise bonus issue meet by leading private sector firm Reliance Industries helped Indian stocks rally from the day's lowest levels to close modestly higher on Thursday, traders said.

"It's been a while since these rumours had been floating and people had sort of given up," said Sanjay Vaid, chief dealer at Bombay's Lloyds Securites. "The news has definitely changed the market sentiment."
The announcement of the bonus meet on June 26 came nearly a year after chairman Dhirubhai Ambani hinted that shareholders were likely to receive a bonus issue in the coming months.
The Reliance spokesman said the firm would meet to finalise a bonus issue of shares on June 26, the day Reliance's annual shareholders' meeting is due.
Reliance has issued two bonus share issues since it was listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on January 23, 1978.
Both times the firm gave investors three bonus shares for every five held. Early speculation in the stockmarket was that the company was likely to maintain this ratio.
"I'm surprised. I was not expecting a bonus," said an analyst at a foreign broking firm. "I didn't think they would do it. They have given very few bonus issues in the past."
